specification.problem: Fixed-point amplitude amplification with quadratic speedup: given A|0>=sqrt(lambda)|good>+sqrt(1-lambda)|bad>, a known lower bound lambda_min, and failure tolerance epsilon, use L=2d+1 oracle queries with Chebyshev-derived phases so the failure probability is <= epsilon for all lambda in [lambda_min,1].
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: A is a single-qubit Ry(2 theta) with sin(theta)=sqrt(lambda), a single good state |1>, L=3 or 5, user-chosen epsilon. The oracle is a phase-parametrized marking, S_s is a phase on A|0>. Phases are computed classically in the Yoder-Low-Chuang form and sin-scan of lambda is run in simulation. The paper's proof of optimality and range-broadness, and the general-n multi-qubit construction, are out of scope.

equations.label: Generalized reflections
equations.description: Phase-parametrized target and start reflections; a=b=pi gives Grover.
equations.justification: Standard generalized amplitude amplification form, given in the sketch.
assumptions: Good state marked by a flag or phase oracle, one query per S_t

equations.label: Query sequence
equations.description: Alternating S_t and S_s with phases chosen by the schedule. The exact ordering and the handling of the extra (L+1)/2 versus (L-1)/2 reflections need to be fixed when implementing, and the final good amplitude is a degree-L polynomial in sqrt(lambda).
equations.justification: The ordering is not stated in the abstract; the sketch only gives L=2d+1 queries.
assumptions: Ordering follows Yoder-Low-Chuang fixed-point search (S_s S_t pairs applied to A|0>)

equations.label: Phase schedule
equations.justification: Recalled from the sketch; the paper's own schedule for the quadratic-speedup version may differ, and the indexing range for j is not fixed here.
assumptions: j runs over 1..(L+1)/2 with the symmetric extension; verify numerically that failure <= epsilon

equations.label: Chebyshev amplitude
equations.description: The good amplitude is a Chebyshev-type polynomial; equiripple |P|>= sqrt(1-epsilon) for x>=sqrt(lambda_min).
equations.abstract_quote: guarantees that this bound is satisfied over the broadest possible range of $\lambda$
equations.justification: Inferred from the claim of an adjustable failure bound over a broadest range; the explicit Chebyshev form is from the sketch.
assumptions: Exact normalization and sign conventions to be fixed numerically

equations.label: Query count and target
equations.description: Query scaling O(lambda_min^{-1/2} log(1/sqrt(epsilon))) and the guarantee to be tested.
equations.abstract_quote: Our result incorporates an adjustable bound on the failure probability
equations.justification: The adjustable failure bound and speedup are in the abstract; the exact L formula is from the sketch and is approximate. Choose the smallest odd L that gives the bound numerically.
assumptions: L rounded up to odd integer

specification.initial_state: |0>^{n} on S, flag and control in |0>

steps.description: Classically compute L, gamma, and the phases alpha_j, beta_j from epsilon and lambda_min.
Prepare A|0> with Ry(2 theta), theta=arcsin(sqrt(lambda)).
Apply L alternations of S_t(alpha_j) (one oracle query each, via controlled-phase on the flag) and S_s(beta_j) (A^dagger, phase on |0>, A).
Scan lambda by varying the Ry angle and compare the good probability with 1-epsilon.

specification.measurement: Measure the S register (or flag) in the computational basis; the good-state probability is the success estimate. Mind Qiskit little-endian ordering.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Estimate P_succ per lambda, check >= 1-epsilon for lambda>=lambda_min.
assumptions: A^dagger free; only S_t placements count as queries
Tiny instance with single-qubit Ry A
Phases are from the Yoder-Low-Chuang form, not verified to be the paper's schedule
